---
title: "Storage and release catalogue design"
---

Current development source includes named remotes, local tree/flat CAS and
explicit verified recovery. The final sections describe implemented local
CSV/JSON history. Earlier dated codec sections record the initial library slices.
Automatic snapshot lookup, ordinary/GitHub new-format integration and optional
DVC remain separate work. Installed preview.3 is unchanged.

## Standalone ordinary use

proj must work with its own native backend without installing DVC. DVC must not
become the mandatory manifest engine or a dependency of ordinary proj use.
Existing interpreter and renderer requirements still apply to selected analyses.

## Optional DVC-backed directories

Future integration may let users opt individual directories into DVC backing.
Only users selecting that integration need DVC. proj should automatically
delegate the appropriate operations at the agreed lifecycle points.

proj retains its logical directory labels/roles and path abstraction regardless
of backend. Integration must preserve label resolution so analysis code does not
depend on DVC-specific physical paths.

DVC remains authoritative for its own tracking and cache state. proj references
the corresponding versions rather than maintaining a second authoritative copy
of DVC's data/cache inventory. Projects should be able to mix native and
DVC-backed directories. Missing DVC, unavailable data and delegation failures
need explicit handling; proj must not silently install DVC.

The directory configuration, supported restore/build/store operations, exact
hook timing and failure/recovery boundaries still need design. This note does
not adopt old command recipes or decide a provider contract.

## A curated release catalogue

The intended release catalogue is a curated, linear history on the main branch,
presented as a readable changelog. A general catalogue of every run on every
branch is not the product goal. This direction does not change current build or
Git branch policies, or remove the need to report failed attempts honestly.

Attempt/release identity, allocation, sealing and how failures relate to this
catalogue remain open. Temporary legacy CSV is approved below. Durable recording architecture,
remote-only discovery, retention and Git-tracking policy remain open; this note
does not claim M2 completion.

See the [behavior contract](behavior.qmd), [current lifecycle](lifecycle.qmd)
and [compatibility log](compatibility.qmd) for implemented behavior and limits.

## Compatible CSV inventory

Status: this CSV implementation is included in published preview.3.
The user approved temporary projr-compatible CSV while broader recording design
continues. This supersedes deferring every manifest implementation.

The root manifest.csv contains quoted string columns in this order:
label,fn,version,hash. The filename is relative to its declared directory with
slash separators, version includes v, and hash is the lowercase MD5 of file bytes.
An empty or absent declared directory has one row with blank filename and hash.
MD5 provides legacy comparison compatibility, not authenticity or security.

Production captures hash-enabled raw/cache directories before analysis, after
start hooks and preparation. Cache capture excludes its framework-owned projr
subtree. After successful output promotion it captures hash-enabled output/docs,
then writes those snapshots followed by prior history. Exact duplicate rows are
omitted; different versions retain records. With no eligible cache the pre-state
stays in memory; otherwise it is also saved at
`<selected-cache>/projr/<release-version>/manifest.csv`. No mapping is invented.
Explicit empty analysis can inventory existing artifacts without claiming analysis ran.

Existing history must have the four columns in order and valid rows; corruption
fails before hooks instead of being discarded. New CSV writes use guarded
same-directory replacement, preserving hard-link aliases. Failure before
publication restores root CSV bytes/presence with managed state. Publication
failure retains the successful local release and CSV. Cache residue may remain.
Previews do not produce production records.

This is an inventory at two lifecycle points, not sealing, environment capture,
immutable attempt identity, concurrent snapshot or complete provenance. End hooks
run later and may change artifacts. The codec is isolated from build capture for
later replacement. CSV has no dependency on CAS. The existing plural
.projr/manifests.csv CAS index and remote JSON/objects remain separate, unchanged.

### Remote layout direction

projr separates provider configuration from latest/archive layouts. Local
providers use `path[/label]` and `path[/label]/v<version>`. Store planning includes
inspection, cues and sync strategies; restore selects available label versions
and copies into final paths. Compatibility includes more than copying a manifest.

Working interpretation: retain ordinary latest/archive and add **CAS as a third
remote structure**, with versioned snapshots and content-addressed objects.
CAS can provide archive storage without becoming the manifest format. Current
Rust runtime now includes ordinary local and GitHub latest/archive publication,
inspection and staged configured restore, plus the older local flat-CAS ingestion
and integrity APIs. Those delivered transfers are not new M3 work. M3 adds the
missing CAS recovery/safety and the now-approved versioned flat/tree metadata;
the first codec slice below does not yet wire new configuration or transfer APIs.
There is no DVC dependency, destructive migration, garbage collection or performance
claim. Ordinary root manifest.csv remains separate from the legacy CAS lookup
ledger .projr/manifests.csv.

Pinned reference:
[manifest](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/manifest.R),
[hashing](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/hash.R),
[build capture](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/build-manifest.R),
[defaults](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/yml-dir.R#L65),
[layouts](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/remote.R#L463),
[store](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/dest-send-label.R),
[restore](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/R/restore.R).

Existing opt-in Git commit behavior still stages eligible project files, including
root CSV unless ignored. This adds no automatic Git requirement or ignore rule.
All regular files, including dotfiles, are inventoried; exact R enumeration parity
beyond the stated schema/capture comparison remains unverified.


## Approved M3 direction and current source boundary

There is one project per store for this milestone. A remote's existing flat CAS
manifest already contains its label, version and all file paths/hashes. The
project-local plural ledger is a lookup shortcut, not the sole holder of that
metadata. Explicit snapshot selection can read remote metadata directly; a
label/version lookup must report missing or conflicting candidates instead of
silently picking one. Automatic discovery improvements and performance tuning
are deferred rather than treated as proof that metadata is absent.

Four choices remain distinct:

| Choice | Meaning | Approved direction |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | How bytes travel | Existing local filesystem or GitHub Releases. |
| Layout | Where payload bytes live | Preserve latest/archive; CAS is an additional structure. |
| Manifest style | How a snapshot's names/content identities are described | flat or recursive tree; defaults flat for GitHub/non-CAS local, tree for CAS; explicit per-remote override. |
| Manifest placement | Where recovery metadata is retained | auto/project/remote/both; auto uses remote for CAS and existing latest/archive behaviour. A small Git root reference can remain even with remote metadata. |

The remotes registry and build.dest selection are approved integration work.
Omitting a selected remote's directory subset means all eligible directories;
removing it from upload targets must not remove it as a restore source. These
new fields are not accepted by the current parser in this codec-only slice.
Legacy configurations and data are not silently converted.

## Versioned codecs in development source

The Rust snapshot_format module introduces three explicit JSON schemas:

- projcli.flat-snapshot.v1: one complete snapshot, with shared version/date
  metadata once and complete file lists grouped by logical label.
- projcli.directory-tree.v1: one directory's direct child name/type/hash entries.
  A child is a file or another tree; no logical label or release metadata is in
  this content object.
- projcli.tree-snapshot.v1: the small version/date and label-to-root associations,
  separate from the directory content IDs.

New file rows name BLAKE3 as their algorithm. Existing ordinary manifest.csv
keeps its four-column MD5 semantics. Existing flat CAS manifests retain their
old label/version-bearing JSON and raw-byte identities; a bare legacy ID is
never automatically interpreted as a new directory tree. This slice adds codecs,
not a destructive conversion or a replacement of either legacy reader.

Flat JSON prints each complete path/hash entry and empty-directory leaf on its
own line. Empty logical roots remain visible even with no files. Other directory
parents are visible in their paths. There are no cross-version deltas or hidden
references needed to inspect the complete flat file list. JSON grouping does not
make this a recursive tree and does not promise smaller files than CSV.

Directory trees bind direct names, file/tree types and child hashes. Changing
a label, build version or supplied date changes snapshot metadata, not the
directory root. A new file changes its content hash and relevant ancestors;
independent unchanged subtrees can retain their IDs. Permissions, ownership and
filesystem timestamps are not part of this byte/name identity.

All new IDs use BLAKE3 derive-key mode with their exact schema string as context,
over compact canonical UTF-8 JSON. Struct fields have fixed order; labels, file
paths, empty-directory leaves and tree children are sorted by UTF-8 bytes.
A supplied RFC3339 date is normalized to UTC; none means unknown and never
queries the clock. Version/date metadata is part of snapshot identity, while
pretty spacing/line endings and input ordering are not. New format versions
must not silently change this canonical encoding.

Readers reject unknown schemas/fields, invalid hashes, duplicate or portable
case/normalization aliases, traversal, device names and conflicting file/empty
directory shapes. Bounds are 16 MiB JSON, 8 MiB text, 100,000 flat entries or
direct children, 4,096 logical labels, 4,096-byte paths with at most 64 components,
and 1,024-byte names/labels. Flat prefix expansion has its own global 16 MiB work
budget checked before allocating derived prefixes.

**Not yet delivered by these codecs:** source ingestion, immutable tree-object
publication, graph traversal/deep verification, restore installation, registry
selection, manifest placement or automatic Git root-reference writes. Those
consumers must verify every object's canonical identity before following
references, bound both graph work and expanded output paths, and publish snapshot
references last. Equal canonical identities must never authorize overwriting
different stored bytes without verified semantic equivalence. Ordinary transfer
and the M2 managed recovery pipeline remain unchanged.

## Targeted lessons, without importing another tool's contract

[Git's objects documentation](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-Objects)
illustrates the separation between file contents, named tree edges and commit
metadata. This is an engineering lesson, not Git-object-format compatibility:
proj's algorithms, encoding and filesystem metadata scope are stated above.

[DVC's cache documentation](https://doc.dvc.org/user-guide/project-structure/internal-files)
shows content deduplication and a directory descriptor containing relative
path/hash entries. Deduplication is independent of whether a manifest is flat
or recursive; grouped JSON alone is not a recursive tree. DVC remains optional
future integration, not a runtime dependency.

[Packit's primary description of outpack packets](https://github.com/mrc-ide/packit)
separates analysis files from associated metadata. Existing M2 attempt/provenance
records serve that different purpose; a content root is not a scientific result,
a complete run catalogue or proof of reproducibility.


## Local tree-object APIs in development source

The cas_tree library now connects the codecs to explicit local storage roots.
This is not new configuration activation or a claim that the CLI can restore
tree snapshots yet. Callers choose a file-content base and a metadata base;
equal bases keep recovery metadata with the content, while different bases
permit project-side metadata without changing content-root IDs.

For a 64-character digest beginning ab, paths are:

| Object | Path below its selected base |
|---|---|
| Raw file bytes, shared with the old CAS | objects/ab/remaining-62-hex |
| V1 directory object | trees/v1/ab/remaining-62-hex.json |
| V1 snapshot reference | tree-snapshots/v1/ab/remaining-62-hex.json |
| Existing legacy flat manifest | manifests/full-64-hex.json, unchanged |

The legacy flat lookup ledger is still project .projr/manifests.csv. New explicit
tree reads do not require it or a working project copy: remote references and
their tree graph contain version/label/name/hash information. The old public
flat verifier remains a separate legacy reader. A missing/empty legacy manifest
directory now fails rather than claiming an archive was verified; an explicit
empty snapshot is valid. Deep legacy errors distinguish missing/nonregular
objects from corrupt bytes.

ingest_directory pre-scans the selected source and rejects links, special files,
unsafe names, source/storage overlap and project control aliases before store
publication. It rechecks each file at open and hashes the same stream that is
copied. It returns an immutable content root, not a published successful snapshot.
It does not silently filter hidden files or produce an atomic consistent image
of a concurrently edited dataset.

publish_snapshot verifies every referenced directory ID and actual file bytes
before atomically installing the immutable reference. Identical supplied
metadata is idempotent. Existing JSON with harmless formatting differences is
validated against the same canonical ID and reused without rewriting it.
Concurrent equal references may converge safely; there is no mutable latest
index or implicit clock in these APIs. Errors can leave unreferenced immutable
objects, not a successful reference to an incomplete graph. No cleanup/GC or
cross-location transaction is promised.

verify_snapshot is read-only and takes an explicit snapshot ID. It checks typed
schemas, object identity, regular/no-link paths and file hashes, and returns
complete observed file/empty-directory membership per label. A small reference
file alone is not sufficient proof that an archive is intact. Metadata is bounded
to 16 MiB per object and 64 MiB unique graph metadata; traversal also caps depth
64, expanded entries 100,000 and expanded path text 16 MiB. DAG reuse does not
bypass the expanded-output limits. Permission/ownership/timestamp restoration and
live-dataset consistency are outside this byte/name observation.

A caller can request a complete readable JSON inventory export, subject to the
separate flat-view bounds. It never substitutes a truncated list. This export
does not select the stored flat catalogue policy.

## Revised flat catalogue direction: CSV and JSON

The later user decision keeps **both** CSV and JSON. Default csv/json catalogues
will deduplicate complete inventories at the logical artefact/version level:
an unchanged later version directly references an earlier complete inventory.
This is distinct from flat/tree structure and raw file-object CAS deduplication.

Optional csv-dedupe-file and json-dedupe-file modes are off by default. Their
dictionary representation must retain every current path membership, resolve
to full verified hashes, and not become omitted-file deltas. CSV must remain
a rectangular Excel-filter-friendly table. A reference row will identify the
earlier complete version; filtering only that later row does not magically
expand the earlier file list.

Those catalogue serializers/reference rules are not wired by this tree-object
slice. The existing complete JSON codec is a full inventory/view primitive;
it is not a JSON-only default or a decision to drop legacy CSV. Existing root
ordinary manifest.csv, old flat CAS data and their readers remain compatible.


## Version-reference catalogue codecs in development source

The new catalogue library keeps **CSV and JSON** and provides four explicit
serialization modes: csv, json, csv-dedupe-file and json-dedupe-file. These codecs
do not yet select a remote's write format, change active configuration, replace
the root projr manifest.csv or migrate existing flat CAS snapshots.

Default csv/json append an unchanged logical artefact as a direct reference to
the earliest complete same-label inventory already in that catalogue. A changed
version has a complete inventory. Reverting to old bytes can reference that older
complete version; references never target other references. Existing records are
not overwritten. Record append order expresses history; no lexical version/date
ordering is inferred. Duplicate label/version records, forward/dangling/cross-label
references and digest mismatches fail.

Inventory equality binds canonical sorted portable paths, entry kinds, full file
BLAKE3 digests and explicit empty-directory leaves. Version, date, logical label
and physical root are outside that inventory digest; reference lookup still
requires the same logical label. The identity domain is
projcli.artefact-inventory.v1 over compact fixed-field JSON containing files and
empty_directories, after the existing flat-path validation. Raw file hashes,
directory-tree IDs and snapshot/reference IDs retain their different domains.

JSON has an explicit projcli.flat-catalogue.v1 schema, format and hash_algorithm.
Each record contains label, version, optional normalized created_at,
inventory_hash and an inventory tagged as complete or reference. A reference has
ref_version and cannot mix in file rows.

CSV has one rectangular header:

schema, format, hash_algorithm, record, record_index, label, version, created_at,
inventory_hash, path, hash, ref_version, file_id.

The record column distinguishes catalogue metadata, inventory, file,
empty_directory, reference and dictionary rows. Explicit inventory rows represent
empty roots too. File membership rows repeat label/version metadata deliberately:
an Excel table filter on a complete artefact/version shows all its file paths.
A reference row names the earlier version to filter; filtering only the later
version does not expand its referenced inventory. record_index keeps append
order explicit even if a spreadsheet sorts rows. CSV quoting preserves commas,
quotes and Unicode rather than changing the recorded path. Import text columns
as text in spreadsheet software; CSV does not control its formula interpretation.

The opt-in file-dedupe modes bundle one dictionary of distinct full file digests.
They retain **every** path membership row, replacing only repeated hashes with
document-local integer file_id values. IDs are assigned deterministically by
sorted full digest for each export; they are not persistent global identities.
Parsing resolves them to full hashes, verifies complete inventory digests and
rejects duplicate/unused/dangling dictionary entries or mixed hash/ID membership.
Exports contain their own dictionary, not references to another database.

These are bounded metadata codecs, not proof that physical objects exist.
Documents cap at 16 MiB, text at 8 MiB, and complete membership/history/dictionary
rows at 100,000; existing path/depth/alias checks still apply. No size or speed
advantage is claimed. Catalogue publication dependency ordering, immutable remote
integration and no-code expanded listing remain integration work.

Independent review tightened the catalogue-wide limits: dictionary plus membership
rows count before JSON expansion, derived path-prefix work shares one 16 MiB
budget across history, and CSV/JSON output stops at the byte limit while writing.
A transient earliest-complete lookup avoids rescanning all history for each new
selected label; it adds no persistent index.


## Verified local tree recovery APIs

The restore_label library API accepts explicit content/metadata bases, a v1
snapshot ID, one exact logical label and an absolute destination whose parent
already exists. It does not infer latest/history candidates or require the old
project ledger. It deeply verifies the full snapshot, materialises selected bytes
into owned private staging, hashes the copied stream and verifies actual private
stage bytes/membership again before replacing the destination.

Recovery reuses the ordinary guarded directory installer and its bounded rollback.
With clear=false, destination-only files survive; matching selected files receive
the selected bytes, and selected empty directories may retain destination-only
children. With clear=true, final membership matches the selected inventory,
including explicit empty directories. The result reports clear and the selected
snapshot/version/label. No project VERSION or source/store bytes are updated.

Project authorities/control aliases, linked/special destinations and overlap with
CAS objects/tree/reference namespaces fail. Empty snapshots need no objects
directory. Remote metadata supports recovery into a fresh empty working project;
project-side metadata remains supported when that metadata still exists.

A new internal installer verification callback runs on its private next-stage
before retaining the previous destination. Existing ordinary local/GitHub paths
use the same installer with their previous behavior. No hard-linked external
file inode is edited in place.

The recovery API remains explicitly selected. Named registry and configured tree
publication/placement are described below; automatic snapshot selection and flat catalogue publication integration remain
pending. Explicit configured verification/recovery is described below.
It is not a crash-atomic transaction or arbitrary concurrent-writer sandbox.
Permissions/ownership restoration is not a CAS guarantee. As with the ordinary
installer, cleanup failure can report an installed destination and retained private
backup rather than pretending rollback after successful installation.


Source review added explicit legacy manifests namespace protection: a tree restore
cannot target the old flat manifests directory either. Merge validation compares
actual directory-entry spelling, including selected empty directories, so native
case aliases cannot widen an existing private directory's modes.

Both private staging levels are explicitly closed. If a pre-replacement callback
rejects a copied tree, cleanup may unlock only owned copies, never the installed
destination or a retained previous original. Primary and cleanup failures remain
visible together; a tree that cannot be safely removed is retained with its path.
The ordinary installer's existing post-install backup-cleanup limitation remains.


## Configured local CAS tree publication (unreleased)

New local CAS definitions can select recursive tree publication through the named
registry. Directory selection is independent of full metadata placement:

~~~yaml
remotes:
  local:
    snapshots:
      path: ../snapshot-store
      structure: cas
      manifest: auto
      manifest-style: tree
build:
  dest:
    snapshots:
      content: [raw, output]
~~~

Omitted content selects eligible non-cache declared labels. Explicit null, false
or an empty list selects none; build subsets cannot enable excluded labels.
auto means remote for this CAS writer. remote stores complete tree objects and
snapshot metadata beside file objects; project stores that metadata under the
project; both requires both copies. File objects always remain in the configured
store. A small project reference is retained for every successful publication,
including remote placement. That reference is not itself a complete archive.

Raw objects, directory objects and snapshot/reference records use first-two-
characters/rest-of-hash fan-out. Identical directory contents share a root across
labels and versions. Snapshot version associations are separate immutable records.
There is no inferred timestamp or mutable discovery index. Existing blobs are
verified before reuse. Required graphs precede full references; the small project
reference is written last. Errors after provider entry retain the local release
and distribution evidence. both is not a cross-location atomic transaction:
partial references/objects may remain and errors say so. Nothing is garbage-
collected or rolled back from a published store automatically.

Previously accepted path/structure/content/inspect CAS definitions keep their
legacy flat JSON identities and plural .projr/manifests.csv ledger. Name-list
selection still works; mapping subsets preserve legacy label spelling. To opt
into new trees, remove the legacy inspect field and explicitly select tree if
desired. No old manifest is reinterpreted or moved.

The first publication slice added tree storage. Explicit named-ID recovery and
local CAS flat CSV/JSON histories are described below. Automatic snapshot lookup
and other-provider formatting remain pending. Legacy inspect belongs only to the
old definition; new manifest-format choices are validated against style. Ordinary
latest/archive and GitHub retain their current metadata policy until separately
integrated; new formatting options are not claimed there.

## Explicit configured tree readers

Named v1 snapshot verification and single-label restore now consider the full
remote and project metadata namespaces independently of current write placement
or style. Current upload content does not hide an explicit historical snapshot.
All present full copies must verify; absence is distinct from corruption. Readers
do not need the old project ledger, root CSV or small project reference.

Selection remains exact title/ID/label, not an automatic newest-version policy.
Existing graph limits and guarded installation are reused. Legacy flat IDs are not recast as v1 tree IDs; the compatibility reader below
restores their original format. Local CAS flat runtime is described below; ordinary/GitHub formatting remains pending.


## Recover existing flat CAS snapshots

The explicit remote verify / remote restore --snapshot commands also read the
original flat JSON snapshots in `manifests/<id>.json`. Their IDs remain BLAKE3 of
the original JSON bytes; they are never reinterpreted as pure content-tree IDs.
Responses identify snapshot_kind as legacy-flat or tree-v1.

The reader validates metadata, portable names and every referenced object before
using the same guarded staging/installer as trees. Old snapshots remain usable
after the remote's current write style changes, without a project CSV or legacy
ledger. Stored metadata, IDs, objects, VERSION and history are never rewritten.

Legacy snapshots record files but not empty directories or permissions. Recovery
does not invent that missing history. Unsafe path aliases, traversal, corrupt or
missing content and conflicting same-ID namespace entries fail explicitly before
destination changes. Metadata is bounded at 16 MiB and 100,000 file entries, with
the existing portable path bounds. Ordinary root manifest.csv remains separate.

Automatic snapshot discovery and ordinary/GitHub formatting remain pending; this is compatibility recovery, not a format conversion or migration.


## Flat history in local CAS

New local CAS remotes can save a readable CSV or JSON history instead of a
directory-tree manifest:

~~~yaml
remotes:
  local:
    snapshots:
      path: ../snapshot-store
      structure: cas
      manifest-style: flat
      manifest-format: csv
      manifest: remote
build:
  dest:
    snapshots:
      content: [raw, output]
~~~

The labels must already be declared. For flat style, csv is the default;
json is also available. Both automatically reuse an earlier complete inventory
for the **same logical folder** when later contents are identical, including a
reversion to older contents. The later version points directly to that earlier
complete version, never a chain. A changed version records all current file
memberships, including additions, removals and renamed paths.

CSV is one rectangular table with a header and repeated label/version columns.
In Excel, filtering a reference version shows the earlier ref_version to inspect;
it does not automatically expand that earlier listing. All earlier complete rows
remain in the same history file. Plain CSV/JSON retains literal full file hashes.
Optional csv-dedupe-file/json-dedupe-file modes replace repeated hashes with a
bundled file dictionary while retaining every file path. These modes are off by
default. They are not omitted-file deltas, and no size/speed advantage is promised.

Files are stored once by their BLAKE3 content hash regardless of manifest format.
Full history files live under catalogues/v1/manifest.csv or manifest.json;
opt-in dictionary files use manifest-dedupe-file.csv/json. Existing root
manifest.csv keeps its separate projr-compatible MD5 schema and is unchanged.

auto means remote for CAS. project/remote/both selects full history placement;
a small project snapshot binding is always retained. Flat bindings connect the
version and selected labels to inventory hashes, independently of serialization
or dictionary IDs. They are not directory-tree object IDs. Full immutable refs
use `flat-snapshots/v1/<first2>/<rest62>.json`; small project refs use
`references/flat-v1/<first2>/<rest62>.json`. No unnecessary tree objects are written.

History replacement is atomic per file. Decoded previous label/version contents
are never overwritten; divergent histories or conflicting same-version retries
fail. Identical per-label retries do not duplicate rows, and missing labels can
resume a partial write. Switching format preserves older files/readability and
uses the longest compatible decoded history; dictionary IDs do not define it.
Codec limits fail explicitly rather than truncating history.

The authoritative history read through replacement/reference publication holds
the existing cooperative claim at `<store>/.proj/build.lock`. Unknown/stale claims
fail closed and only an owned claim is removed; there is no automatic process
killing or stale-claim cleanup. Raw immutable objects may be copied before that
claim. Required history copies precede full snapshot refs, then the small project
ref. both is not a cross-location transaction: errors can leave objects or an
updated first history copy. Retry can finish the remaining copy.

Explicit verify/restore resolves version references/dictionaries, checks inventory
hashes and actual raw bytes, and uses the existing guarded installer. The result
reports snapshot_kind: flat-catalogue-v1. Old tree and legacy-flat IDs stay distinct
and readable, regardless of the current write style. A small binding alone is not
a backup. Empty directories are recorded by this new format, unlike legacy flat.

These new manifest-format controls currently apply to local CAS. Ordinary local
latest/archive and GitHub Release providers retain their existing metadata path;
their new-format integration is still pending. Trees default to fixed v1 JSON;
explicit manifest-format: json is valid there, while CSV/dictionary choices require
flat style. Null/unknown modes fail instead of silently choosing a default.


## Ordinary local history integration (development source)

Ordinary latest/archive data keeps its existing directory layout; new flat
catalogues do not copy files into objects. A distinct versioned local binding
records each logical folder's inventory hash, relative physical payload path,
empty flag and existing VERSION advertisement. Its ID is a snapshot binding,
not a pure content root. Small project references persist with remote-only full
metadata. One archive payload may serve several build-version observations.
Mutable latest storage cannot promise recovery of older overwritten content.


## GitHub flat history integration (development source)

GitHub full catalogue/history and snapshot bindings share the versioned
projcli-manifests-v1.zip asset; data stays in the ordinary ZIP layout. Bindings
include frozen repository/tag and the actual payload asset, separate from the
build-version inventory. Exact prepared ZIP observations preserve existing
packaging semantics rather than inventing empty directories. Disk-backed private
records avoid retaining full metadata buffers for every target at once.

Every required HTTP write and full project copy precedes small project references.
Original asset-ID checks protect against replacing an already changed history;
they do not establish cross-writer or crash atomicity. No CAS objects, new
credential mechanism, live user-data test or broad snapshot discovery is introduced.
